start.name: El Sheikh Zuweid (الشيخ زويد / Ash Sheikh Zuwayyed) town center
start.coord_basis: OSM place=town node for the real North Sinai town of Sheikh Zuweid (pop. ~60,000), which matches GEM's StartLocation 'El Sheikhh Zowayed' and the Arabic segment name خط غاز الشيخ زويد. This is a town-level anchor (acceptable per brief § rules since no separate metering-station/tie-in name was found in any source) -- not necessarily the exact pipeline take-off point; see flags.

end.name: Sinia Cement Industrial Area (El Hassana cement cluster, North Sinai)
end.coord_basis: Center of an OSM landuse=industrial polygon (way 97684492, source=bing) that directly overlaps an independently-tagged OSM 'Sinai White Cement Factory' works node (id 11306179852, ~600 m away) in the El Hassana area of central North Sinai -- the cement-manufacturing cluster housing Sinai Cement Company (Vicat subsidiary) and Sinai White Portland Cement Co. Sinai Cement Company's own corporate site (sinaicement.com) independently confirms it operates 'a state-of-the-art plant in North Sinai' (no further precision given there). Matches sheet's EndPrefecture/District 'Sinia Cement Industrial Area'.

prior_passes.notes: Searched: EGAS Annual Report 2018 full text (via Wayback, no hits for these names); OSM/Overpass for 'Sheikh Zuweid' place node (found, high confidence) and for cement works/industrial-landuse features in the 30.5-31.0N/33.5-34.2E box (found two clusters, ~8km apart, matching the two-plant story implied by P8052/P8053's two segments); web search + sinaicement.com (Sinai Cement Company's own corporate page, Cairo HQ address only, generic 'North Sinai' plant confirmation, no coordinates). I deliberately avoided a set of search-engine summaries that were themselves paraphrasing gem.wiki content (standing rule 1 -- never cite or rely on GEM as evidence) and relied only on OSM + the company's own site instead. Confidence tier: MEDIUM on the identity of both named places (2 independent non-GEM sources: OSM + sinaicement.com corroborate the existence and rough location of a North Sinai Sinai-Cement plant cluster; OSM alone for Sheikh Zuweid town, which is uncontroversial); LOW on the length/diameter/commissioning facts (single, unverifiable-in-text citation) and on whether the town center is the true pipeline terminus given the length-implausible flag above.

staged_now.researcher_notes: No ENTSOG coverage in North Sinai (NO_NETWORK_MATCH; nearest nodes 17-30 km).  A short industrial spur running inland/south from the North Sinai coastal town of Sheikh Zuweid to the El Hassana cement-manufacturing cluster in central North Sinai -- almost certainly a tap off the larger 36in national-grid 'Trans-Sinai' trunk (see P8055 notes) that runs roughly El-Qantara--El-Arish through this same interior corridor, since a coastal town like Sheikh Zuweid would not itself be a gas source. No map or route document naming the actual corridor path (vs. a straight line) was found.  Searched: EGAS Annual Report 2018 full text (via Wayback, no hits for these names); OSM/Overpass for 'Sheikh Zuweid' place node (found, high confidence) and for cement works/industrial-landuse features in the 30.5-31.0N/33.5-34.2E box (found two clusters, ~8km apart, matching the two-plant story implied by P8052/P8053's two segments); web search + sinaicement.com (Sinai Cement Company's own corporate page, Cairo HQ address only, generic 'North Sinai' plant confirmation, no coordinates). I deliberately avoided a set of search-engine summaries that were themselves paraphrasing gem.wiki content (standing rule 1 -- never cite or rely on GEM as evidence) and relied only on OSM + the company's own site instead. Confidence tier: MEDIUM on the identity of both named places (2 independent non-GEM sources: OSM + sinaicement.com corroborate the existence and rough location of a North Sinai Sinai-Cement plant cluster; OSM alone for Sheikh Zuweid town, which is uncontroversial); LOW on the length/diameter/commissioning facts (single, unverifiable-in-text citation) and on whether the town center is the true pipeline terminus given the length-implausible flag above.  FLAG: length-implausible: straight-line distance between the best-available endpoints (Sheikh Zuweid town center to the Sinia Cement industrial area, El Hassana) is ~62.98 km, which EXCEEDS the sheet's stated 45 km pipe length (ratio 1.40x) -- physically impossible, since a pipeline's actual route length can never be shorter than the straight-line distance between its true endpoints. Either GEM's 45 km figure is understated, or 'El Sheikhh Zowayed' denotes a specific tie-in/metering station on a trunk line that sits well south of the town itself (Sheikh Zuweid is a real, distinct coastal settlement ~63 km northeast of El Hassana) rather than the town center used here. No primary source pinning an exact tie-in point was found.  FLAG: unverified-in-seed-source: the EGAS Annual Report 2018, the sheet's cited [ref] for Status/Length/Diameter/PipelineType/Location on this row, does not contain any text match for this pipeline's name, endpoints, or length when full-text searched (see facts.source) -- the citation may be miscited or refer to imagery/tables not captured by OCR/text extraction.  FLAG: duplicate-pipelinename-two-pids: P8052 and P8053 share the exact PipelineName 'El Sheikhh Zowayed-Sinia Cement Gas Pipeline' but are separate ProjectIDs/segments (24in vs 16in, 45km vs 16km, different endpoints) -- functionally this looks like ONE multi-segment pipeline (Sheikh Zuweid -> Sinai Cement -> Military Cement) split across two rows. Worth a GEM data-model review: either that's intentional segment-per-PID granularity (fine) or these should be tied together as one PipelineName with two SegmentName rows under a shared network/parent construct, consistent with how GEM otherwise tracks multi-segment lines.

staged_now.researcher_notes: No ENTSOG coverage in North Sinai (NO_NETWORK_MATCH; nearest nodes ~29-30 km).  A short industrial-to-industrial spur (~7-8 km straight-line) linking two separate cement clusters in the same central-North-Sinai heavy-industry belt south of El-Arish: the civilian Sinai Cement Company / Sinai White Cement complex at El Hassana, and the NSPO-owned ('military') El-Areesh Company for Cement plant at Jabal Lubna, further east/southeast toward El-Arish. Both sit off the same interior road network south of the El-Qantara-El-Arish corridor; no published map of the specific pipe route (vs. straight line) was found.  Same search process as P8052 (see that entry for the EGAS report / OSM / cement-cluster methodology). Additionally checked NSPO's own site (nspo.com.eg/nspo/cement.html) directly, which independently corroborates the 'military cement' identification and its Jabal Lubna / south-of-El-Arish location -- this is a genuinely independent, non-GEM primary source (the plant owner's own page), giving reasonably solid confidence in the END point identity specifically. Confidence tier: MEDIUM-HIGH on the identity of 'Military Cement' = NSPO's El-Areesh Company for Cement (owner's own site + OSM agree); MEDIUM on the Sinia Cement Industrial Area start point (same basis as P8052); LOW on the 16km/16in facts themselves (unverifiable in the cited source).  FLAG: length-plausible-but-high: straight-line distance between the Sinia Cement industrial area (El Hassana) and Military Cement (Jabal Lubna) is ~7.4 km vs. the sheet's stated 16 km -- a ratio of ~2.17x actual-length-to-straight-line. This is NOT the physically-impossible case (unlike P8052), but it is a wide margin for a short industrial spur between two nearby sites; flagging per the brief's guidance since it exceeds the ~1.4x comparison threshold. Plausible explanations: genuine road/terrain routing detour, or (less likely) one of the two industrial-area anchors is imprecise.  FLAG: unverified-in-seed-source: see P8052 -- the cited EGAS Annual Report 2018 has no full-text match for this segment.  FLAG: duplicate-pipelinename-two-pids: see P8052's flag -- P8052 and P8053 are two segments of what functionally reads as one continuous multi-leg pipeline (Sheikh Zuweid -> Sinai Cement -> Military Cement), filed as two separate ProjectIDs under an identical PipelineName. Flagging for the same GEM data-model question raised on P8052.

prior_passes.sheet_conflicts: StartLocation and EndLocation are blank on the sheet. StartState/Province and EndState/Province are both 'Sinia' — this is a misspelling/transliteration of 'Sinai' (Arabic سيناء), NOT صينية, El-Saff, or Sinnuris. Confirmed independently: GASCO's own EGPC-published progress reports (Petroleum Magazine, Dec-2024 and Nov-2025 issues) describe a project called 'خط إزدواج عبر سيناء' ('Trans-Sinai duplication line'), 36-inch diameter — the Dec-2024 issue states this 15 km segment was completed and gas flow began 2024/6/8, matching P8008 (36in, 15.5km, StartYear1=2024, StartMonth1=6) almost exactly. THIS PIPELINE IS IN/NEAR THE SINAI PENINSULA, NOT UPPER EGYPT — it appears to have been mis-scoped into this 'research_payload_upper_egypt.json' batch. Recommend re-routing to a Sinai/Suez-Canal-region batch.
prior_passes.notes: 'Sinia' resolved: it is GASCO's own transliteration convention for 'Sinai' (compare EndState/Province='Sinia' also used elsewhere in the same GGIT snapshot for the unrelated 'Trans Gulf Gas Pipeline', StartLocation='Petreco Plant' — confirming 'Sinia' is a recurring sheet spelling for the Sinai Peninsula, not a one-off typo). The Arabic project name 'ازدواج سيناء' means 'Sinai duplication/twinning' — i.e. this is additional (looped/parallel) pipe added alongside an existing Trans-Sinai gas transmission corridor for capacity, not a new standalone route. Two candidate PARENT corridors were found (either could be what's being duplicated, or it could be a different unlisted stretch): (1) GASCO's 'El Tina – Abu Sultan Onshore Gas Pipeline' (32-inch, 60 km, built ~2005–06, financed via EIB) — a 2005 Environmental Impact Assessment gives its exact valve-room endpoints: starts at a valve room north of the Al Qantara–Fakous road (32°15'20"E, 30°49'50"N) and ties in at a valve room north of the Abu Sultan–Cairo road (32°09'28"E, 30°23'50"N) — this runs on the WEST bank of the Suez Canal (Ismailia/Sharqia), feeding Abu Sultan and Ataqa power stations and 'supporting the Oyoun Mossa pipeline' (which continues into Sinai proper). (2) The separately-reported 'Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline', El-Tina East to El-Arish, ~111 km, explicitly on the Sinai (east) side and also described as a capacity-duplication project. I could NOT confirm which of these (or which specific km-stretch) the 15.5 km P8008 segment corresponds to, so no defensible two-point endpoint pair could be sourced — marking unresolved rather than guessing. Diameter (36in) and both segments' lengths (15/15.5 km and 28/27 km) match the sheet closely enough to firmly confirm PID identity even without a route. Recommend: (a) re-scope this PID out of the Upper Egypt batch, (b) if pursued, search Egyptian contractor/EPC press releases (Petrojet, Enppi, Orascom Construction) for the specific 'ازدواج عبر سيناء' contract announcement, which sometimes names exact valve-room tie-ins the way the El Tina–Abu Sultan EIA did. Note: this session's web-search quota was exhausted while researching this PID; further search would need a fresh session.

THIRD PASS — still unresolved; no facility-level endpoint found for P8008 (GASCO's 36-inch 'khat izdiwaj 'abr Sinai' line #1, 15/15.5 km, gas flow started 2024-06-08, i.e. already complete). This pass had a working WebSearch tool from the start (confirmed with a first test query in Arabic before doing anything else), so it is not limited to the WebFetch-only workaround the first two passes used, though WebFetch itself still 403s on several Egyptian outlets (akhbarelyom, in particular) and had to be routed through the r.jina.ai text-extraction proxy (curl -L https://r.jina.ai/<url>) to get readable text — noted here so a future pass doesn't waste a cycle rediscovering the same WebFetch failure mode. Ran ~20 additional Arabic-language WebSearch queries this pass combining 'ازدواج خط عبر سيناء' / 'خط ازدواج الغاز' with جاسكو, بتروجت, إنبي, أوراسكوم, named North Sinai markaz/village candidates (الرومانة، القنطرة، بئر العبد، الشيخ زويد), an EEAA/environmental-consultation angle, and a direct search for GASCO's own site (gasco.com.eg) and the official Ministry of Petroleum press portal. New source found and fetched this pass: the Ministry of Petroleum's own press release for GASCO's 2024 general assembly (https://www.petroleum.gov.eg/ar-eg/media-center/news/news-pages/Pages/mop_04032024_02.aspx, dated 2024-03-04) — verbatim confirms 'استكمال مشروع إزدواج خط عبر سيناء 36 بوصة ومخطط الانتهاء فى أبريل 2024' (completion of the 36-inch Trans-Sinai duplication line project, planned completion April 2024) alongside other GASCO trunk projects (Al-Tina West/Mit Nama 167km 42in, Sulaimaniya/North Giza 42in, Fayoum feeders). This is a strong CORROBORATING primary-government source for P8008's existence/spec/timing (now 3 independent sources: this Ministry release, the GASCO Dec-2024 Petroleum Magazine annual report already in the payload, and general-assembly wire coverage), but like every other source found across three passes it gives NO route, station, km-point, or village name for this specific 15/15.5 km segment. Also specifically checked whether either of the two North Sinai Governorate/GASCO/Eco Conserve items found this pass (see P8009 notes) could pertain to P8008 instead of P8009: both are explicitly framed as ongoing/pre-construction activity (crop-damage compensation for a project still requiring field assessment as of 2026-04-07; a community consultation on 2025-11-18) — impossible for a line that already completed and flowed gas on 2024-06-08. That inference from pass 2 is reconfirmed, not just repeated. No new candidate corridor-stretch information surfaced (the EIB 2007 EIA's LOOP#1/LOOP#2 km-ranges and the pre-2020 134km two-phase duplication remain exactly as characterized in pass 2 — nothing ties either to P8008's specific 15/15.5km). Marking unresolved rather than guessing a stretch of the 111km 'Abr Sinai' corridor. NOT attempted/exhausted candidates for a future pass: GASCO's own Facebook page (could not access via WebSearch/WebFetch/jina — Facebook requires login and returned no crawlable public post history through any available tool this pass); a direct EEAA (eeaa.gov.eg) portal search for a 2024 (not 2025) scoping/EIA filing specific to phase 1, which — if it exists — should predate the ministry's April-2024 completion target and could name termini the way the 2007 EIB EIA for the original corridor did.

Confirmed independently across two GASCO annual reports (Petroleum Magazine Dec-2024 and Nov-2025): diameter (36in) and both segments' lengths (15/15.5 km and 27–28 km) match P8008/P8009 closely enough to firmly confirm PID identity even without a route.
prior_passes.notes: RETRY PASS — additional research, still unresolved. This session's WebSearch tool hit its per-session query budget again before any query ran (same limitation the prior pass hit), so this pass worked entirely through WebFetch against DuckDuckGo/Bing HTML result pages plus direct curl+pdftotext downloads of primary documents — a workaround, not a dead end. New findings this pass: (1) A community/environmental consultation session on 2025-11-18, organized by North Sinai Governorate at the invitation of GASCO and the environmental consultancy Eco Conserve, covered 'khat izdiwaj al-ghaz bi-shamal Sinai' (the North Sinai gas-line duplication project) — https://almessa.gomhuriaonline.com/626213/ and https://akhbarelyom.com/news/newdetails/4727064/1/. Both articles confirm the companies and North Sinai Governorate location but give no route/km/facility detail. Since P8008 already completed and flowed gas on 2024-06-08 (well before this Nov-2025 consultation), this consultation almost certainly pertains only to the still-under-construction P8009, not P8008 — P8008 is not tied to a fresh EIA/consultation record found anywhere. (2) Downloaded and full-text-searched the EIB EIA for the historically related 'GASCO Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' (El-Tina East–El-Arish, 111 km, 32in, EIB project 20070088, PETROSAFE, Nov-2007) — https://www.eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_eia2_en.pdf. That original design already contained two internal 'LOOP' (duplicate-pipe) sections: LOOP#1 from the start point (km 00+00, agricultural area near El-Sheikh Gaber Canal, west-of-canal side) to km 32+00–33+00 near Romana villages; LOOP#2 from roughly km 84 to the km 111 end point near El-Midan Village (km 102–103) and on to El-Arish. This shows looping/duplicating this exact corridor is a recurring GASCO engineering pattern going back to 2007, but nothing ties the 2024/2025 'izdiwaj' projects to this specific 2007 EIA's loop segments — they could be new loops laid decades later at different km ranges, and no source states which. (3) Found (via Wayback Machine, since the live page now 404s/redirects) a 2020 soutalomma.com article confirming an EARLIER, separate 'Trans-Sinai gas line duplication' totaling 134 km built in two phases, explicitly to serve Sinai's own local consumption — establishing this is a recurring multi-decade capacity-expansion program on the corridor, not a one-off, but again with no named endpoints. (4) EcoConserv's public oil-and-gas project portfolio (ecoconserv.com/oil-gas/) lists several other GASCO EIA jobs (Raven pipeline, Giza North, Dahshour-Atfeeh, Nubaria-Metnama) but nothing Sinai-specific, consistent with the Nov-2025 consultation being too recent to be listed yet. No source anywhere names a specific facility, valve room, or km-point for the 15/15.5 km P8008 segment. Marking unresolved rather than guessing a corridor stretch. Recommended next steps for a future pass: (a) request the EEAA/Eco Conserve scoping document for the Nov-2025 consultation directly (it will very likely give exact km-point termini once public); (b) search the Ministry of Petroleum's and GASCO's own Facebook pages around 2024-06-08 for an inauguration post (these frequently name both tie-in stations); (c) if a fresh session restores WebSearch, target Petrojet/Enppi/Orascom Construction EPC contract-award announcements for 'khat izdiwaj 'abr Sinai'.

staged_now.researcher_notes: The seed source (GASCO's 2024 'National Natural Gas Grid Expansion Projects' deck; the live URL 404s, recovered via a Wayback snapshot with a URL-encoded filename) names this project 'Duplication of the Trans-Sinai pipeline' -- 28 km, 36in, project location 'Sinai' (governorate field, singular), cost 631 million EGP / USD 13,000,000, status 'Under Study'. The cost figure (USD 13,000,000) matches the sheet's ProjectLevelCost exactly, confirming this is unambiguously the right GASCO line item for P8055. But GASCO names no towns or stations -- it is explicitly a DUPLICATION (a parallel/looped second pipe) of an EXISTING Trans-Sinai trunk, not a description of a new, independent corridor. That existing trunk is a 36in, ~196 km line, per EGAS's own 2018 Annual Report, which lists (under pipelines needing rehabilitation) a 'Project Rehabilitation gas supply pipeline Trans-Sinai Pipeline 36"-196 km' with no route detail given either. A related, better-documented project -- GASCO's Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline EIA (a separate, 111 km line, El-Tina East to El-Arish, cited in the brief) -- describes its own route running parallel to 'the existed Abr Sinai old pipeline' and to 'an existed pipeline' along the El-Qantara-El-Areish desert road, crossing the El-Sheikh Gaber Canal near El-Qantara. This is circumstantial support that the broader 'Trans-Sinai' trunk corridor runs roughly El-Qantara (Suez Canal / Ismailia Governorate side) eastward to El-Arish -- but nothing in any source I could reach names which specific 28 km stretch of that ~196 km corridor GASCO is duplicating, so I have NOT picked coordinates for either end. Given the diameter/cost match is exact but the two named administrative units in GEM's own StartState/EndState ('Sinia' / 'Suez') don't line up with GASCO's single-governorate 'Sinai' location field, I would guess (without evidence) that the duplicated stretch is near the WESTERN, Suez-Canal-crossing end of the trunk (i.e. near El-Qantara) rather than the El-Arish end, since that is the only plausible reading that could produce a 'Suez'-adjacent terminus -- but this is a guess I am explicitly NOT turning into coordinates.
